text: Confirmed: `Interval.fromISO` calls `DateTime.fromISO` on both halves before knowing which half is a duration, so with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` the duration half throws `InvalidArgumentError` instead of falling through to the Duration branch. A subagent is fixing it now (wrap the DateTime parses so a failed parse doesn't throw) and running the interval + full test suites to make sure nothing else breaks. ETA ~10 min.

Got it. Year 0100 is not a leap year in the proleptic Gregorian calendar, so day 61 of 0100 is March 2 — the result suggests leap-year / days-in-month handling is wrong somewhere around the year-100 boundary. A second subagent is on it now (root cause + fix + full test suite). ETA ~12 min. Bug #1 fix is still in progress.

On it — a third subagent is investigating `isInDST` (likely the DST-detection logic in the zone implementation, not a hardcoded 1974 issue) and will fix the root cause plus run the zone and full test suites. ETA ~12 min. Bugs #1 and #2 are still being worked.

Bug #1 is fixed and verified. Cause: `Interval.fromISO` eagerly parsed both halves with `DateTime.fromISO`, and with `throwOnInvalid = true` `DateTime.invalid()` throws instead of returning an invalid DateTime, so the duration half blew up before the Duration branch was reached. Fix in src/interval.js: each DateTime parse is wrapped in try/catch (a throw counts as "not valid"), and the Duration parses are guarded the same way so genuinely unparsable input still reaches `Interval.invalid("unparsable", ...)` (which throws InvalidIntervalError when throwOnInvalid is set). Verified: `"2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M"` and `"PT5H30M/2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00"` now return the same valid intervals as with the default setting; behavior with throwOnInvalid=false unchanged; test/interval suite 127/127 passing and the full suite has no new failures (only the 2 pre-existing toFormat ICU/locale failures).

Thanks — a fourth subagent is now on the `Duration.normalize()` NaN bug (likely in the unit-conversion matrix / normalization logic in src/duration.js and src/impl). It will fix the root cause, check related unit combinations, and run the duration + full test suites. ETA ~12 min. Bugs #2 and #3 are still in progress.

Understood — the year padding code is treating the `-` sign as a digit. A fifth subagent is fixing the root cause so all negative-year ISO output is correct (`-0001-01-01`, `-0010-01-01`, etc.) without changing positive-year output, and running the datetime + full suites. ETA ~12 min. Bugs #2, #3 and #4 are still in progress.

Got it — `FixedOffsetZone` should reject non-numeric offsets and make DateTimes built with it invalid with reason \"unsupported zone\". A sixth subagent is on it, keeping valid fixed offsets working as before, and running the zones + full suites. ETA ~12 min. Bugs #2–#5 are still in progress.

Bug #5 is fixed and verified. Cause: `padStart` in src/impl/util.js padded the whole string form of the number, so the leading `-` counted as one of the digits (`padStart(-1, 4)` → `"00-1"`). Fix: pad the magnitude and prepend the sign separately, matching Intl's `minimumIntegerDigits` semantics. Now `-1` → `-0001-01-01`, `-10` → `-0010-01-01`, `-100` → `-0100-01-01`, `-999` → `-0999-01-01` (and toISO/toISOWeekDate/toFormat/toRFC2822/Interval output all follow). A sweep of years -12345…118040 across 39 format tokens plus all ISO/JSON/RFC/HTTP outputs shows only negative-year lines changed — year 0 and every positive year are byte-identical. Full suite: 892 passed / 2 failed, the same 2 pre-existing French-ICU `toFormat` failures as before the fix.

Bug #4 is fixed and verified. Cause: the conversion matrices in src/duration.js were incomplete — `casualMatrix.years` had no `quarters` entry and `casualMatrix.quarters` had no `seconds` entry (same gap in `accurateMatrix.years`), so `convert()` read `undefined` and produced NaN. Fix: added the three missing entries (`years.quarters: 4`, `quarters.seconds: 91*24*60*60`), consistent with the surrounding matrix. Now `{years:1,quarters:2}` → `{years:1,quarters:2}` with `as("years")` → 1.5, `{quarters:1,seconds:2}` no longer NaN, and `{quarters:1}.as("seconds")` → 7862400 (was silently 0). An exhaustive 9×9 unit-pair sweep × {casual, longterm} shows no NaN and no missing matrix entries; a 744-output before/after snapshot diffed to only the 18 previously-NaN/silently-0 entries. Duration suite 114/114 passing; full suite unchanged (892 passed, same 2 pre-existing French-ICU toFormat failures).

Bug #6 is fixed and verified. Cause: `FixedOffsetZone` hard-coded `get isValid() { return true; }`, so a non-numeric offset like `"CDT"` was accepted; DateTime only emits `"unsupported zone"` when `!zone.isValid`, so the bogus zone slipped through and the DateTime ended up invalid with reason `"invalid input"` instead. Fix (src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js): `isValid` now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`. Now `new FixedOffsetZone("CDT").isValid === false`, and `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone })` is invalid with reason `"unsupported zone"` (explanation: `the zone "UTC-NaN" is not supported`). All valid offsets are unchanged (`utcInstance`, `instance(360)` → "UTC+6", `instance(-390)` → "UTC-6:30", `parseSpecifier("UTC+6")`, zone strings "utc"/"GMT"/"Etc/GMT+5", fromISO/fromRFC2822/fromFormat offset parsing). Zones suite 32/32 passing; full suite unchanged (892 passed, same 2 pre-existing French-ICU toFormat failures).
